messages:
incident-bot: Pager P1 triggered for service: serving-runtime-high-dropchain / rule: ib_dropchain_surge. Alarm details: host-group=rack-7, metric=ib_dropchain, value=2376. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ib-loss

sarah: oncall here — acknowledged. pulling logs and metrics now :eyes:

mike: seeing 5xx spike from frontends -> backend pool 'serve-us-west1'. 5m agg: 8.0% 5xx, p95 latency 2.6s (baseline 150ms)

priya: quick note — a bunch of redwood-server pods are restarting with exit code 137, plus CUDA errors in container logs. pasting snippet:

```
[2026-03-15T18:03:21Z] redwood-server[23456]: runtime error: cudaErrorIllegalAddress
[2026-03-15T18:03:21Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 23456 (redwood-server)
[2026-03-15T18:03:22Z] kubernetes: container restarted (exitCode=137)
```

yuki: running IB counters on rack-7-node-14:

```
# ibv_devinfo -v
hca_id: mlx5_0
port:1
  state: ACTIVE
  phys_state: LINK_UP
  link_layer: InfiniBand
port:2
  state: ACTIVE
  phys_state: LINK_UP
  link_layer: InfiniBand

# cat /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/ports/2/counters/port_xmit_discards
port_xmit_discards: 19234
port_rcv_errors: 4821
qp1: dropchain_inc=1830
qp2: dropchain_inc=2190
```

mike: that matches. Looks like packet loss causing GDR/driver to misbehave and provoking GPU-side faults -> memory corruption -> OOMs.

sarah: customer impact — region us-west1 affected. Support-surface: ~13% of API calls for a subset of customers returned 502/503 in last 10m (estimated). High-volume PLG customers and a couple enterprise customers in the region. Rob — any escalations?

rob: yep, three elevated tickets and one live chat from an enterprise account (acct: ENTERPRISE-ALPHA). I'll open a status update after we have an ETA. Drafting now.

priya: mitigation plan I'm rolling: 1) cordon+drain rack-7-node-14 2) model fallback to quantized variants for hot routes 3) reduce max batch sizes to limit memory pressure. Starting drain now.

```
kubectl cordon rack-7-node-14
kubectl drain rack-7-node-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
redwoodctl route set-fallback --route=/v1/chat --variant=quantized-1 --percent=10
```

yuki: will run live IB checks and coordinate with dc-noc. quick test packet snap via tcpdump shows apparent retransmit storms. also running a simple qperf to test IB bandwidth/latency.

mike: planning a targeted driver restart on node-14 during a low-traffic window; postponing until drains finish. driver restart command (linux):

```
modprobe -r nv_peer_mem mlx5_core
modprobe mlx5_core
modprobe nv_peer_mem
```

Note: this will briefly interrupt GPU RDMA paths for pods on that host.

sarah: approved. Priya — after drain confirm, go ahead with driver restart. Yuki — please open ticket with switch team; sounds like microbursts on EOM buffer causing port-level retransmit.

yuki: opened ticket #DC-4821 with switch team; tagging NOC and HW-oncall. asked them to check switch buffer counters and ECMP behavior. Also suggested temporarily reducing MTU from 4096 -> 2048 on affected nodes as a quick test.

priya: canary started: quantized-1 at 10% for /v1/chat. early signals: 5xx on canary down ~50% (small sample). rolling to 30% now.

mike: driver restart completed on rack-7-node-14 at +12m. node rejoined, kubelets healthy. Observed two additional pod evictions (OOMKill) during drain window; adjusted REDWOOD_MAX_BATCH.

```
kubectl set env deployment/redwood-serve REDWOOD_MAX_BATCH=64
```

priya: after batch limit + quantized canary, region 5xx dropped from 8.0% -> 1.2% over last 5m. p95 returned to ~240ms. continuing to monitor.

rob: sent initial customer notice to affected accounts. Copy:

"We're investigating network-related disruptions affecting inference in US-West. Our engineers are mitigating and routing traffic to healthy capacity. We expect improvement within 30-60 minutes. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."

yuki: Switch team reported microbursts on leaf-12 causing ECMP hashing instability and per-path queue overflow. They rebalanced flows and patched switch buffer settings. They also noted one port experienced repeated micro flaps at 23:54 UTC.

sarah: good. For now incident state -> MITIGATED but monitoring. leaving pager open for 60m to ensure stability. Postmortem owners: mike (infra) + yuki (network). Priya to own runbook updates and model-fallback playbook. Rob to follow up with customer comms.

priya: will capture timeline and reproduce steps for runbook; adding note to disable aggressive GDR fallback until switch teams confirm stable link behavior.

mike: capturing logs and exporting dmesg/kern logs to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/4123456789/artifacts

sarah: thanks team. next update in 30m or on significant change. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident 4123456789 state changed -> MITIGATED (monitoring). Pager remains open for 60m. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ib-loss
